speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, please describe exactly where the pain is located and how severe it is on a scale of 1 to 10. Additionally, have you noticed any fever, chills, nausea, or changes in your urination such as frequency or urgency?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To better characterize the right flank pain and rule out infection, could you describe if the pain comes in waves, radiates to your groin, or if you have any fevers? Additionally, have you noticed any clots in your urine or a history of kidney stones?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nephrolithiasis (Right Kidney Stone). Based on the classic presentation of hematuria, right flank pain, and a history of recurrent UTIs, this is highly suggestive of a stone causing obstruction and secondary infection. I recommend a Non-Contrast CT KUB for confirmation and to assess stone size.
